standard.title: Technology, Living Standards, and Environmental Concern in the 20th Century
standard.description: changing historical perspectives over time in relation to the developments in technology, public health, longevity, standard of living in the 20th century, and concern for the environment and sustainability
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have studied significant historical changes in technology, society and the environment in earlier periods, including the industrial revolution and early 20th century technological change.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify changing historical perspectives on technology, public health, standard of living and environmental concern across the 20th century, explaining how each domain changed and how attitudes to each shifted over time.

nodes.label: Technological developments since 1945
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify key technological developments since 1945 and explain how each changed historical perspectives on standard of living and daily life.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least three technological developments since 1945 across at least two domains (household, travel/trade, communications) and explain how each changed daily life.
nodes.typical_width: Identify key developments in technology since 1945 across the following areas: the household — television, appliances, central heating and cooling; travel and trade — shipping and passenger jets; globalisation, mass consumption and communications — the microchip, satellites and digital systems; explain how each development changed historical perspectives on standard of living and what was considered a normal or good life.
wider: Trace the development of digital communications technology from the microchip through personal computing to the internet and social media, examining how each step changed not just what people could do but how they understood their connection to the wider world

Compare the distribution of technological benefits globally — examining how access to household technology, travel, and communications has been unequally distributed across income levels and between high-income and low-income countries

response_modes.reason: Students need a working knowledge of the range of post-war technological changes before they can meaningfully analyse shifting historical perspectives. A domain-organised inventory (household, travel, communications) builds this repertoire efficiently.

success_criteria: Identify at least three technological developments since 1945 from at least two different domains
Explain how at least two of these developments changed daily life and historical perspectives on standard of living
Describe how communications technology in particular changed how people related to the wider world

nodes.label: Population growth and public health
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can discuss the growth in the world's population during the 20th century, including changes in life expectancy and the depletion of natural resources.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe the pattern of world population growth during the 20th century and explain at least two causes or consequences.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss the growth in world population during the 20th century — from approximately 1.6 billion in 1900 to 6 billion by 2000; including life expectancy changes in different parts of the world (dramatic increases in high-income countries, more variable improvements in low-income countries); the depletion of natural resources as a consequence of population growth and industrialisation.
wider: Compare life expectancy improvements in high-income vs low-income countries, examining what the data reveals about how the benefits of 20th-century medical and technological progress were distributed
Investigate the concept of ecological overshoot — examining how resource depletion and population growth have combined to raise questions about the sustainability of 20th-century development patterns

response_modes.reason: Population growth and life expectancy are most meaningfully understood through comparative data. Use graphs comparing different regions and time periods — the differential between high-income and low-income countries is the analytically important insight, not the aggregate global figure alone.

success_criteria: Describe the pattern of world population growth during the 20th century
Explain at least two causes or consequences of 20th-century population growth
Describe how life expectancy changed across the 20th century and identify at least one factor that explains variation between different parts of the world

nodes.label: The environmental movement
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how the rise of the environmental movement changed historical perspectives on renewable energy, sustainability, and the relationship between human activity and the natural environment.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain how the rise of the environmental movement changed perspectives on at least one specific issue (e.g. renewable energy, recycling, species protection).
nodes.typical_width: Identify how the rise of the environmental movement around the world changed people's perspectives on renewable energy technology and sustainability measures such as recycling; connect the movement's rise to the conditions that enabled it (population increase, urbanisation, industrial pollution, species extinction); trace how environmental awareness shifted from fringe concern to mainstream policy agenda across the second half of the 20th century.
wider: Trace the development of Australian environmentalism from the Franklin Dam campaign (1982–1983) to contemporary climate activism, examining how the movement's strategies, mainstream acceptance, and targets have changed over four decades

Examine the Apollo 8 'Earthrise' photograph (1968) as a turning-point moment in environmental consciousness, investigating how a single image changed how people understood the relationship between humanity and the planet

response_modes.reason: This node integrates the technological and demographic changes of Nodes 1 and 2 with the environmental movement — connecting the unintended consequences of technological progress and population growth to the emergence of sustainability as a historical perspective and policy imperative.

success_criteria: Explain how the rise of the environmental movement changed perspectives on at least one environmental issue
Identify at least two conditions that enabled the growth of the environmental movement
Describe how environmental awareness became a mainstream policy concern across the second half of the 20th century
